small_guidance:
- The ConvTranspose2d call dominates runtime (cuDNN on a 16×64×512×512 input producing 16×128×514×514). Tuning the mean/finalize kernels further has near-zero headroom — fast_p is already ~1.02. Try increasing BLOCK to 8192 and SPLIT to 16 with num_warps=8, num_stages=3 to reduce launch overhead, but expect marginal gains.
- Consider running the conv_transpose on channels_last memory format (`y = self.conv_transpose(x.to(memory_format=torch.channels_last))`) so cuDNN selects a faster algorithm on Ada; then have the mean kernel iterate with stride-aware indexing.
- Fuse the partial-mean and finalize into a single persistent kernel per N (one program reduces all OC×HW), eliminating the partial buffer round-trip — small win since the conv is the bottleneck.
large_guidance:
- Replace nn.ConvTranspose2d with a custom Triton scatter-add kernel: with kernel_size=3, stride=1, padding=0, each input pixel contributes to a 3×3 patch in the output. Tile over (N, OC tile, output spatial tile) and loop over IC and the 3×3 kernel positions, doing a GEMM-style accumulation — this is where ~95% of the 20ms lives and where any real speedup must come from.
- Alternatively, since output is only padded by 2 on each side (H_out=514), formulate it as a regular conv: cross-correlate the zero-padded input (pad=2) against the flipped weight — this maps cleanly to an im2col-tiled GEMM kernel which is easier to write than scatter-add and matches the conv-transpose output exactly.
- Fuse the global mean into the conv-transpose epilogue: each (N, OC) program accumulates its output tile straight into a per-(N,OC) running sum register, never writing the 16×128×514×514 intermediate (~2.1 GB) to HBM. Then a tiny second kernel does bias-add + logsumexp + ×10. This removes the dominant memory-traffic cost.
